stem:
On a hot afternoon, Chitra watches dark thunderstorm clouds build over heated fields. The air above the fields is warm and moist.

Which sequence correctly explains how the thunderstorm develops?

options.text: Heated land warms the moist air; the warm air rises and creates low pressure; cooler air flows in; the rising air cools and its water vapour condenses into clouds and rain.
Warm moist air warms the heated land; the land rises and creates low pressure; cooler air flows in; water vapour condenses into clouds and rain.
Heated land warms dry air; the dry air rises and creates low pressure; cooler air flows in; clouds and rain form without moist air.
The same chain produces a thunderstorm even when the air above the fields is cool and dry.

teacher.key_rationale: Heated land warms moist air; rising air makes low pressure; cooler air flows in; rising moist air cools and condenses into clouds and rain. B swaps which body rises. C drops the moist-air condition. D applies the rule when air is cool and dry.
